label: Thomas Aquinas, Sententia libri…: Every POTENCY_1 is of the contradictory: whatever is in…
interpretation: Aquinas' proof that no sempiternal being is in potency: every potency is at once of the contradictory (omnis potentia simul est contradictionis), said of passive potency, by which a thing is possible to be and not to be, simply or in a respect (n. 2); what is possible to be can also not be in act (n. 3); what can not be is corruptible, simply or in the respect in which it can not be, as a body that can fail to be in a place is corruptible in place (n. 4): 'Relinquitur ergo, quod omne quod est in potentia, inquantum huiusmodi, corruptibile est.' Read per respect in the case's vocabulary: whatever is in potency in r can fail to be r (CanFailToBe x r). The reading does not make potency in an accidental respect a capacity to fail to be in substance, and it encodes 'can' as a primitive, not as quantification over situations.
